subject: tasselled wobbegong shark
title: A Shark Swallowed Another Shark Whole, Head First, and Just Lay There

scenes.text: Divers found a shark with another shark inside it. Both were still in one piece.
August 2011, Great Keppel Island on the Great Barrier Reef. Two scientists counting fish swam over a tasselled wobbegong.
Sticking out of its mouth was the tail of a bamboo shark. The wobbegong was 1.3 meters long. Its meal was a meter.
They watched for 30 minutes. Neither shark moved. The wobbegong was swallowing a fish three quarters its own length, head first.
Wobbegongs are carpet sharks. They lie flat on the seabed, fringed like weed, and wait. Prey swims too close and the jaws snap shut.
Those jaws can dislocate to swallow things almost as big as the shark itself. It was the first time anyone had photographed it eating another shark.

description:
On 1 August 2011, researchers Daniela Ceccarelli and David Williams were counting fish off Great Keppel Island on the southern Great Barrier Reef when they found a tasselled wobbegong about 1.3 metres long swallowing a brown-banded bamboo shark about 1 metre long, head first.
They watched for about 30 minutes and neither animal moved. Wobbegongs are camouflaged ambush predators whose jaws can dislocate to take large prey whole; stomach studies had shown they eat other sharks, but this was the first published photograph of it. The observation appeared in the journal Coral Reefs in 2012.
What is the strangest thing you have seen an animal eat? Tell us below.
first_comment: The researcher who found it said she doubted it was the first time it had happened, only the first time anyone had a camera. Which ocean predator should we cover next?
